chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan narrated from his brother Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from his father, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from Yahya ibn Ya'la, from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ribat, from Mansur ibn Hazim, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who made a will bequeathing more than one-third, and his heirs were witnesses who approved of that for him. He said, 'It is valid.' Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ribat said, 'And in my view, this is on the condition that they were pleased with it during his lifetime and acknowledged it.'

key_terms.الثُّلُث: One-third (standard limit for wills without heir consent)
key_terms.شُهُودٌ: Witnesses (here implying heirs present and consenting)

ai.seo_question: Is a will exceeding one-third valid if the heirs agree?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates a will exceeding the standard one-third limit upon the heirs' consent, a ruling that underscores the principle of *ridwan* (pleasure/agreement) in Shia inheritance jurisprudence. The narrator Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ribat clarifies that this consent must be explicit and given during the testator's lifetime, distinguishing it from posthumous approval. This highlights the flexibility of *mawarith* (inheritance) rules when the heirs voluntarily waive their rights, reflecting the Quranic emphasis on mutual agreement in financial matters.
